intro: Two threads run through my work. Each step draws on the ones before, both in what I built and in how I tested and reported it. Projects that stand on their own are listed separately.

threads.title: Biosignals
threads.subtitle: From a breadboard amplifier to statistically tested brain-signal analysis

steps.built: Built an ECG front end on a breadboard, one stage at a time.
steps.evidence: Compared each stage with its design value.

steps.built: Designed gate-level logic that cross-checks ECG and pulse-oximeter heart rate.
steps.evidence: Tested each block against expected outputs.

steps.built: Turned a muscle signal into motion: analogue EMG, firmware and a 3D-printed hand.
steps.evidence: Reported prototype measurements as indicative, not verified.

steps.built: Built and tested a participant-level machine-learning pipeline for prefrontal fNIRS.
steps.evidence: Designed validation in from the start and reported results with their statistical limits.

threads.title: Medtech translation
threads.subtitle: From a clinical workflow to a regulatory and commercial route

steps.built: Automated post-operative follow-up for patient-specific implants.
steps.evidence: Mapped each assessment to its own score bands, keeping named instruments separate from custom sections.

steps.built: Built the adoption and fundraising case for a fracture-healing monitor.
steps.evidence: Kept the concept separate from evidence that does not exist yet.

steps.built: Mapped a research robot's route to a CE mark under the EU MDR.
steps.evidence: Tested each classification rule against the device, with a reason.
